newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens Medical OK'd for one-for-two scrip issue.
newsitem.headline: Athens Medical OK'd for one-for-two scrip issue.

text.p: Athens Medical Centre got shareholder approval on Thursday for a one-for-two scrip issue, capitalising reserves amounting to 662.5 million drachmas.

Company president George Apostolopoulos told shareholders at the annual general meeting that pretax earnings were forecast to grow at an average 22.5 percent between 1996 and 2001 and reach 9.0 billion drachmas from 4.2 billion in 1996.
In the first five months of 1997, Athens Medical Centre's pretax earnings were up 29.4 percent year-on-year to 2.045 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 14.8 percent to 6.207 billion.
He anticipated the company will turn in an average turnover growth rate of 11.6 percent in the five years to 2001, from 12.8 billion drachmas to 22.1 billion.

On a consolidated basis, profit was seen growing at an average 38.5 percent to 18.5 billion drachmas in 2001 from 3.9 billion in 1996. Over the same period, turnover is expected to grow by 32 percent to 55.15 billion drachmas from 15.6 billion.

Management said it negotiated a syndicated 8.0 billion drachma loan facility, with syndicators including the European Investment Bank (EIB) which has so far refrained from lending to the medical services sector.
Syndicated loans would be provided at Athibor or Libor plus 1.0 percent.

Shareholders were also told that negotiations for the set up of a diagnostic centre in FYROM and a clinic in Montenegro had reached a final stage, while an agreement had been struck for the operation of a clinic in Athens' western suburb of Peristeri.
Management also revealed plans for a controlling stake in a provider of hospital management services to Greece's public and private medical sector.
Athens Medical Centre will distribute a dividend per share of 100 drachmas for fiscal 1996, up from 80 drachmas a year earlier.
Its shares shall trade ex-dividend and ex-bonus June 27. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
